title: Plan it
about: The page in this film is real: an agent drew it from one sentence and the app as it stands, and it is shown as it was written. It is the first half of a planning session. The owner has not answered it yet.

lines.text: Before anything is described to the framework, you talk the system through, until it fits on one page.
It starts with one sentence, in your words. Here is a real one, for the next stage of Plugged In.
People should be able to pay each other by name. A handle gets a wallet, and anyone can send money to that name.
That is all the designer is given. That, and the app as it stands.
The first thing a designer does is say your idea back, as strongly as it can.
A claimed name becomes a place money can be sent. Every claimed handle has one wallet.
And it says what the idea is not. Not a bank. Not a checkout. Not an exchange.
Then it draws the system: the things, and the states each can be in. A wallet. A payment. A withdrawal.
Then, the rules. What must stay true, in your language.
A name has at most one open wallet.
Money sent to a name reaches the person who held it when it was sent. Never a later one.
You might never have said that second rule aloud. It decides what happens when a name changes hands with a payment on its way. That is what the page is for.

scenes.title: What waits, and what must agree

lines.text: Two parts of the page are where real systems go wrong.
The first is anything that waits. On the page, it's a thing in a state, and it says what it is waiting for. A wallet, opening, waits for the money provider.
The second is every place two records of one fact must agree. The app's balance, and the money the provider really holds.
A plan is finished when it says what it doesn't know.
Seven doubts. Each one is a question, and each is sorted. Try it in throwaway code. Or leave it blank, for you to decide.
And it asks one question first. Is this real money, and if so, who holds it while it sits in a wallet?
One honest note. This page is real, and it is half a session. The owner hasn't answered yet, so nothing on it is decided.
No command runs any of this. It's how we plan, and it is practice. Next: the doubts become spikes.
